headline: MCA reportedly proposes NFRA recruitment changes; deputation tenure may rise to 7 years
summary_points: Business Standard reports that MCA has proposed changes to recruitment norms at the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA).
The deputation tenure at NFRA may reportedly be extended to 7 years.
Only the headline is available; full details of the proposal, such as posts covered and the status of the draft, are not confirmed.
No notification or draft rules have been quoted in the report; this is a proposal, not a final rule.
who_is_affected: NFRA staff and prospective deputationists, along with government departments and professionals who may be considered for NFRA roles.
action_required: Watch the MCA website for the draft or final notification and review the official text before relying on the reported changes.

MCA has reportedly proposed changes to recruitment at the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), including a possible increase in deputation tenure to 7 years, according to Business Standard.

What is reported:
- Recruitment norms at NFRA may be revised.
- Deputation tenure may rise to 7 years.

What is not yet clear:
- The posts covered and the exact mechanism.
- Whether this is a draft for comments or a final decision.

NFRA is the regulator overseeing auditing and accounting standards for companies and audit firms, so staffing rules may influence its capacity and functioning. At this stage, this is a press report and no notification number has been quoted.

Professionals interested in NFRA roles or in the evolving regulatory framework should track the official notification when it is released.

Please verify the details with the official MCA and NFRA sources before acting on this update.
